commit.message:
release v0.10.0: the prose lane consults the LEXICON (plan/0044, host-lint #16)

The --prose and --docs lanes now mask a sanctioned LEXICON phrase before the
host-grammar density engine, the same pre-detection blank-out the naming lane
performs. A declared multi-word domain phrase clears the trope within it, while a
standalone occurrence of the word still flags. The mask feeds both the per-tell
scan and the document density score, so a declared phrase contributes to neither.

scan_prose_text and run_docs take the allow-list; the README masked-modes wording
adds --prose and --docs. Two unit tests and two integration cases pin the
behaviour. Closes host-lint #16.

commit.message:
the walk names what it could not read, and the gate judges the record

Three defects on the documents walk, all found by the agentic-host plan/0078
convening and each reproduced before it was fixed.

A document the walk listed and could not open was dropped by a bare
`if let Ok(content)`, and the run still reported clean. A tracked file carrying
a real tell, made unreadable, yielded `prose: clean` at exit 0. The walk now
returns what it could not read and every gating caller refuses. This is the
coverage class agentic-host plan/0077 closed for its reference sweep and left
open here.

`run_docs` now takes the corpus it judges. The hook keeps the working tree,
because catching a document before it is staged is its job (host-lint#17); a
gate takes the record, because reddening over an uncommitted note asserts
something about a tree no clone contains, and it blocked a release over a file
the release does not ship.

`--all <dir>` and `--docs <dir>` pushed the directory onto the file list and
never read it, so the walk audited whichever tree the working directory
resolved to and returned a confident verdict about a tree it was not handed.
One directory is now honoured and anything else is refused.

Reverting each fix fails its own test and no other.

commit.message:
host-lint: flag decoration tells on the commit subject line

A decoration tell (em/en-dash, smart quote, arrow) is advisory prose
everywhere except the first line of a --stdin scan: the commit subject
or gh title, which becomes the squash-merge subject and front-door text.
There a single decoration char is the tell, not rhetoric, so it
escalates from warn to flag (exit 1). Body prose and --prose docs are
unchanged. Spec rule FlagSubjectDecoration + obligations + tests;
VOCABULARY records the exception.

commit.message:
feat: add a history scan mode for auditing existing repos (#6)

* feat: add a history scan mode for auditing existing repos

Hooks gate only new commits and rules grow over time, so adopting or
upgrading the skill in an existing repo left no way to ask what the
current rules would flag in content already committed.

Add --log: runs each commit message from git log through the engine,
labelling findings with the short sha. Document the one-shot
adoption/upgrade audit recipe (--all for live files, --log as an
informational history scan) in README and SKILL.md, with integration
coverage in a throwaway repo.

Fixes #5

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: make history cleanup an opt-in archive-then-rewrite flow

History findings stay informational by default, but the audit now
guides an explicit remediation path: archive the original history on
a pushed branch, then amend the tip or rebase/filter-repo deeper
commits and force-push with lease, noting the sha-churn cost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: link replaced commits to their rewrites with a trailer note

After an archive-then-rewrite cleanup, each replaced commit gets a
Superseded-by trailer attached via git notes (and refs/notes/commits
is pushed), so the archived sha points at its replacement without
itself being rewritten.

commit.message:
document the corpus, generated from the table the checker reads

RULES.md is produced by make-rules-doc.sh from src/rules.rs, so the human form and
the checker's table cannot drift apart, and a CI job regenerates it and diffs: a
difference means somebody edited the document instead of the registry, which is how
a rule table starts lying.

The first version of that script was a stub that printed a message and regenerated
nothing while the document claimed it did, which is the same defect this project
retired a promised-but-unimplemented key for. It generates now, idempotently.

Getting the document past the prose gate produced one instance of a failure recorded
earlier in this session: replacing em-dashes mechanically left a sentence
ungrammatical. That one is repaired, and the substitution was checked for others
rather than assumed clean.

host-lint 0.4.1: honor .host-lintignore in per-file scans; exclude self-corpus

A tell detector flags its own corpus, so the hygiene lane could not gate this
repo without --no-verify — a methodology gap (host#?, surfaced here).

  from the hook, and fixtures no longer need --no-verify to land.
- .host-lintignore: exclude the validated self-corpus (VOCABULARY.md/README/SKILL =
  the spec + docs; test-integration.sh/lint-skill.sh = test-harness scripts;
  tests/ = proptest fixtures). Each was checked line-by-line; src/lib.rs stays
  scanned (2 example comments reworded so it warns, never flags).
- test-integration.sh: fix 4 stale assertions — subject-line decoration flags (not

- Patch release: a CI/hook-affecting fix warrants a 0.0.1 bump + tag. Rolls up the

commit.message:
the series lane, over the order the commits land in

Checks that only exist across commits: whether a consumer lands before its
provider, whether a registration brought its obligations, whether a backport
candidate stayed focused.

Two corrections the node called for and the original design lacked. The
generated-header allowlist decides whether this lane is usable at all:
config_components.h is written by configure and is never in the tree, so a
provider check demanding its source would flag every series that includes one.
And provider-before-consumer extends to Makefile object references, which is the
form that matters most: a build listing foo.o before foo.c exists is broken at
exactly the commit a bisect lands on, so that one is mechanical rather than
advisory.

Registration triggers cover every table, including filters and bitstream filters,
because a check knowing only codecs and formats never fires on a new filter at
all. Each obligation fires separately so an author is told which of Changelog,
doc and MAINTAINERS is missing rather than that something is.

Must-pass holds: FLAG=0 across 60 windows of five accepted commits, with 33 clean
and 27 carrying advisories.

commit.message:
host-lint 0.7.0: host-lint:ignore fenced blocks skip literal tell-citations (call/0019)

The markdown naming scan skips a fenced code block whose info string is
host-lint:ignore, so a doc can reproduce a tell-shaped token literally (a
retired-ordinal dictionary, an archived citation) without flagging — the idiomatic
markdown info-string pattern (like a mermaid block), deliberate and source-visible,
never --no-verify. The prose scan already skipped fenced blocks. Boundaries: markdown
only; tagged blocks only (a regular fence, or a rust/text tag, is still scanned);
blocks not inline (an inline backtick still flags, so a tell cannot be laundered).
Specced (below the spec, like masking), tested, documented per plan/0027.

commit.message:
encode the FFmpeg rule corpus, pinned and self-checking

26 rules over the five rule-bearing sections of doc/developer.texi, each naming
the section and subheading it comes from, pinned to FFmpeg master c6309b5c with
a digest per section and per source file.

Three separations that carry the weight. Sources are pinned whole so a fetch can
be checked; sections are digested individually so drift localises to what moved
rather than reporting 'the file changed'; and rules name their subheading so a
rule with no upstream source cannot exist. Drift in a section that states no
rules is reported and does not gate, because upstream re-indenting its Vim recipe
is not rule drift and a check that cried wolf on every unrelated commit would
stop being read.

measured_rate is None on every rule and a test refuses any value: a tier is a
claim about detectability, and the calibration node measures it. A number nobody
measured reads as evidence, which is worse than an empty field.

SHA-256 is written out rather than depended on, because the vendored bundle and
the reproducible build are anchored to this crate having no crates.io
dependencies. Checked against the FIPS 180-4 vectors including the empty string,
and across every length spanning the block boundary where a padding bug lives.

The registry checks itself at runtime, not only under test: an unmapped
rule-bearing section or a rule naming no section refuses rather than presenting
an incomplete corpus as the corpus. The Forge lane variant is removed until the
forge-lane node has a rule for it; a variant nothing constructs is a promise the
corpus does not keep.

Cross-checked independently: the digests were generated in Python and the Rust
splitter and hasher agree over all 35 sections of the real file.
